s0301.literal: That day, he died at the Hall of Awakening Consciousness.
s0301.idiomatic: That same day he died in Youjue Hall.

s0302.literal: The testament edict said: "I am ill and lingering near death, reaching the point of no recovery; long and short life have their allotted span—what more is there to say?
s0302.idiomatic: His death edict read: "My illness lingers without relief and has reached what medicine cannot cure; length of days is ordained—what more can I say?

s0303.literal: Only the royal enterprise is arduous; year after year there are campaigns; the living people are much afflicted—do not forget shame and caution.
s0303.idiomatic: Yet the throne's work is hard, campaigns come year after year, and the people bear many wounds—never lose your sense of shame and care.

s0304.literal: Now the regions are only just settled, popular teaching is not yet spread abroad, and I meet the great decline—it is a regret left behind.
s0304.idiomatic: The realm has only just been pacified and custom and learning are not yet abroad, yet I approach my end—that is my regret.

s0305.literal: The altars of soil and grain bear heavy responsibility; the Crown Prince may immediately assume rule; kings, marquises, generals, and ministers—well assist and support; inner and outer in harmony—do not go against my intent!
s0305.idiomatic: The state rests on heavy shoulders: let the crown prince take the throne at once; let princes and ministers aid him well; keep court and command united and do not stray from my wish.

s0306.literal: The mountain tomb should be kept frugal and swift.
s0306.idiomatic: Keep my tomb plain and the burial swift.

s0307.literal: When the great encoffining is finished, the hundred officials shall attend once every three days; the regulations for removing public mourning—all follow the old statutes."
s0307.idiomatic: After the laying in state, ministers shall attend every three days; rules for ending public mourning shall follow the old code."

s0308.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi day, the hundred officials presented the posthumous title Emperor Wen, temple name Shizu (Founding Ancestor).
s0308.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi day, the ministers offered the posthumous name Emperor Wen and temple name Shizu.

s0309.literal: On jingyin day, he was buried at Yongning Mausoleum.
s0309.idiomatic: On jingyin day he was interred at Yongning Mausoleum.

s0310.literal: Emperor Wen rose from hardship and knew the people's suffering.
s0310.idiomatic: Emperor Wen came up through hardship and understood the people's distress.

s0311.literal: State expenditures strove for thrift and restraint.
s0311.idiomatic: State spending was kept spare and frugal.

s0312.literal: In regular levies and collections, when affairs could not be avoided, he would surely sigh and change countenance, as if upon his own person.
s0312.idiomatic: Whenever unavoidable levies had to be ordered, he sighed and his face fell as if the burden were his own.

s0313.literal: When the responsible official presented decisions, he finely discerned truth and falsehood; below him deceit found no place, and people knew to encourage themselves.
s0313.idiomatic: He reviewed memorials with a keen eye for truth and fraud; subordinates could not cheat, and men learned to discipline themselves.

s0314.literal: In one night those who pierced the inner quarters to fetch external affairs for separate judgment came one after another without cease.
s0314.idiomatic: Night after night messengers came from the inner gate bearing outside business for him to decide.

s0315.literal: Whenever the cock herald waited on the clepsydra and passed the night tally into the hall, he then ordered the deliverer to cast the tally upon the step-stone so that it rang with a clang, saying, "Though I sleep, I shall also be made to start awake."
s0315.idiomatic: Each time the night herald brought the watch tally to the hall, he ordered it thrown onto the stone steps with a sharp clatter, saying, "Even in sleep I want to be roused."

s0316.literal: From beginning to end his stern integrity—such instances were many.
s0316.idiomatic: His firm character showed in many such ways from first to last.

s0317.literal: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: The world speaks of succeeding the bodily succession and guarding the written canon, of collateral branches inheriting the line—the gaps between gain and loss, it may be said, are also fully set forth.
s0317.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: The world judges heirs who keep the founder's way and branches that carry on the line, and the record of success and failure is long.

s0318.literal: In general, to uphold and not let fall is deemed worthy ability; to bend and easily change it is deemed unworthy.
s0318.idiomatic: In general, to hold the legacy without letting it slip counts as talent; to warp or lightly change it counts as failure.

s0319.literal: Those who can glorify the former track and bear the weight of what ancestors built are indeed few.
s0319.idiomatic: Those who brighten their forebears' path and bear up the work of earlier builders are few indeed.

s0320.literal: Emperor Wen from his first setting forth, merit and achievement were conspicuous; he pacified disorder and quieted marauders, first assisting the great enterprise.
s0320.idiomatic: From his first rise Emperor Wen's deeds were plain: he stilled rebellion, quieted enemies, and stood at the head of the founding effort.

s0321.literal: When the state's calamity suddenly arrived, he entered to receive the precious throne, cautious and fearful, as if driving rotten wood.
s0321.idiomatic: When disaster struck the realm and he took the throne, he was cautious and uneasy, as one who drives a rotted axle.

s0322.literal: [24] Moreover he revered Confucian learning, loved and delighted in literary principle, saw good as if he could not reach it, employed men as if through himself, used respectful frugality to govern his person and diligence to aid things—of old the paragons of civil and martial virtue, the queens who sighed east and west on campaign—the traces of guest and essence could be joined in kind.
s0322.idiomatic: [24] He honored Confucian learning and loved letters, pursued good as if he could never catch it, and chose men as if for himself; he ruled his own life with modest frugality and labored for the people's good. He belongs in the company of rulers true in wen and wu and of consorts whose campaigns won both praise and lament—the pattern fits the finest models of old.

s0323.literal: As for wielding intelligence and employing discernment, that is the government of Yongping—the former histories have discussed it in those terms.
s0323.idiomatic: In wielding talent and sound judgment he matched the Yongping reign of Han; the histories say as much.

s0325.literal: By merit he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander over ten commanderies including Kuaiji, General Who Proclaims Martial Valor, and Governor of Kuaiji—comment: in the edict text of the Basic Annals of the Founder, Part Two, for the bingchen day of the eleventh month of the first year of Yongding, "Bearer of the Staff" reads "Bearer of the Staff with Credential."
s0325.idiomatic: On "by merit appointed Bearer of the Staff, commander of ten Kuaiji-region commanderies, General Who Proclaims Martial Valor, governor of Kuaiji": the Founder's annals for Yongding 1/11/bingchen read Bearer of the Staff with Credential.

s0326.literal: Separately there was the rank of Marquis of Changcheng County; this is not written here.
s0326.idiomatic: He also held the rank of Marquis of Changcheng County, omitted here.

s0327.literal: General Who Pacifies the South, Opener of the Mansion with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Zhou Di was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South—comment:
s0327.idiomatic: On "General Who Pacifies the South, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes Zhou Di advanced to General Who Garrisons the South"—note:

s0329.literal: "General Who Garrisons the South" reads "General Who Pacifies the South."
s0329.idiomatic: reads General Who Pacifies the South.

s0330.literal: On gengxu day Prince Bamao was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing—comment:
s0330.idiomatic: On "gengxu day Prince Bamao was enfeoffed Prince of Shixing"—note:

s0332.literal: , his receiving the enfeoffment was in the tenth month of the third year of Yongding; here it says the eighth month, gengxu day—it differs from the biography.
s0332.idiomatic: his enfeoffment came in the tenth month of Yongding year 3; this entry's eighth month, gengxu day disagrees with the biography.

s0333.literal: Changing the enfeoffment of the Heir of Shixing, Prince Xu, to Prince of Ancheng: "Xu" originally read "taboo name"—probably Yao Cha's original text was thus; now according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions it is changed.
s0333.idiomatic: On "transferring the Shixing heir Prince Xu to Prince of Ancheng": the text originally read taboo name, preserving Yao Cha's wording; emended per the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions.

s0334.literal: Hereafter when such cases occur, collation notes are not all fully given.
s0334.idiomatic: Similar cases below are not all noted in full.

s0335.literal: On xinyou day of the ninth month Prince Bozong was established as Crown Prince—comment: "ninth month, xinyou day" in the Basic Annals of the Deposed Emperor reads "eighth month, gengxu day."
s0335.idiomatic: On "ninth month, xinyou day, Prince Bozong was made crown prince": the Deposed Emperor's annals read eighth month, gengxu day.

s0336.literal: Exultation flowed among the common folk: "exultation" was originally corrupted to "clap hands"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
s0336.idiomatic: On "exultation flowed among the common folk": the text originally read clap for exult; other editions are correct; emended.

s0337.literal: Also alike in bestowing amnesty: "bestow" was originally corrupted to "bow"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
s0337.idiomatic: On "also alike in bestowing amnesty": the text originally read bow for bestow; other editions are correct; emended.

s0338.literal: Jiangning was already the old burial ground: "was"—the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read "had."
s0338.idiomatic: On "Jiangning was already the old burial ground": the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read had for was.

s0339.literal: Making oaks and unhewn timber bear songs: "song (ge)"—Yuan Gui 813 reads "song (ge)."
s0339.idiomatic: On "making oaks and rough timber bear song": Yuan Gui 813 reads song (歌).

s0340.literal: Comment: ge is the ancient character for song; below, "song-bells arrayed in the storehouse treasury" is the same.
s0340.idiomatic: Note: ge is the archaic form of song; the same applies to song-bells in the storehouse treasury below.

s0341.literal: Broadening the net and cautious punishment: "cautious"—all editions read "reduce."
s0341.idiomatic: On "broadening the net and cautious punishment": all editions read reduce for cautious (眘).

s0342.literal: Comment: shen is the ancient character for cautious; those who read "reduce" are suspected of later arbitrary emendation.
s0342.idiomatic: Note: shen is the old form of cautious; reduce looks like a later guess.

s0343.literal: Dispatching Ba Province Inspector Hou Anding to garrison it: "Hou Anding"—all editions read "Hou Andu."
s0343.idiomatic: On "dispatching Ba Province Inspector Hou Anding to hold it": all editions read Hou Andu.

s0346.literal: says: "At the time Hou Andu as Minister of Works joined Hou Tian on the southern campaign and had never been Ba Province inspector—Hou Anding must be a different person."
s0346.idiomatic: writes: "At the time Hou Andu as minister of works joined Hou Tian on the southern campaign and had never been Ba Province inspector—Hou Anding must be someone else."

s0347.literal: He Province Inspector Pei Jinghui fled to Qi: "Pei Jinghui"—the Book of Northern Qi and the Biography of Wang Lin in the History of the Southern Dynasties both read "Pei Jinghui (variant character)."
s0347.idiomatic: On "He Province Inspector Pei Jinghui fled to Qi": the Book of Northern Qi and the Wang Lin biography in the Southern Dynasties annals both read Pei Jinghui (暉).

s0348.literal: Dingchou day—comment: that year in the third month dingwei was the first day of the month; there was no dingchou; lacuna suspected.
s0348.idiomatic: On dingchou day: that year the third month began on dingwei—no dingchou occurs; date doubtful.

s0349.literal: Winter, tenth month, yisi day: "yisi"—the Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "guichou."
s0349.idiomatic: On "winter, tenth month, yisi day": the Southern Dynasties Annals of Chen Emperor Wen read guichou.

s0350.literal: Comment: that year in the tenth month guiyou was the first day of the month; there was neither yisi nor guichou; lacuna suspected.
s0350.idiomatic: That year the tenth month began on guiyou—neither yisi nor guichou fits; date doubtful.

s0351.literal: Tianjia year 3, Goguryeo King Gao Tang—or some editions read "Gao Yang."
s0351.idiomatic: Tianjia year 3, Goguryeo king Gao Tang; some texts read Gao Yang.

s0352.literal: Minister of Works Hou Andu defeated Liu Yi at Taozhi Ridge: "Taozhi Ridge"
s0352.idiomatic: On "Minister of Works Hou Andu defeated Liu Yi at Taozhi Ridge"—note:

s0355.literal: Appointing General Who Pacifies the South Hua Jiao as Inspector of South Xiangzhou—Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies among the Twenty-two Histories says: "The main biography only says Inspector of Xiangzhou; the character 'South' is suspected to be intrusive."
s0355.idiomatic: On "appointing General Who Pacifies the South Hua Jiao inspector of South Xiangzhou": Qian Daxin holds the biography reads only Xiangzhou inspector and that South is probably intrusive.

s0356.literal: On xinyou day a comet appeared—comment: above in the Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu in the History of the Southern Dynasties there are the two characters "sixth month"—here omitted.
s0356.idiomatic: On "xinyou day a comet appeared": the Southern Dynasties Annals of Chen Emperor Wen place sixth month before xinyou; it is omitted here.

s0357.literal: Comment: according to the Treatise on Astronomy in the Book of Sui, in the sixth month of Tianjia year 6 of Chen, on xinyou day, there was a comet more than a zhang in length.
s0357.idiomatic: The Sui Treatise on Astronomy records a comet over a zhang long on xinyou of the sixth month, Chen Tianjia year 6.

s0358.literal: Linchuan Governor Luo Wenya beheaded Zhou Di—Qian Daxin's Examination says: "The main biography and the Biography of Chen Baoying only call him 'Luo Ya.'"
s0358.idiomatic: On "Linchuan governor Luo Wenya beheaded Zhou Di": Qian Daxin notes the biographies call him only Luo Ya.

s0359.literal: As for their ordering the realm
s0359.idiomatic: As for their governance of the realm

s0361.literal: [Wang] enterprise—according to the Southern Supervisory edition and Yuan Gui 191 it is changed.
s0361.idiomatic: On [Wang] enterprise: emended per the Southern Supervisory edition and Yuan Gui 191.

s0362.literal: What age lacks talent: "talent"—Yuan Gui 191 reads "it."
s0362.idiomatic: On "what age lacks talent": Yuan Gui 191 reads it for talent.

s0363.literal: Comment: reading "it" gives the longer sense.

s0364.literal: Still practiced the [rites of] Qi and Song
s0364.idiomatic: still observed the rites of Qi and Song

s0366.literal: [state]—according to the Southern Supervisory edition and Yuan Gui 191 it is changed.
s0366.idiomatic: On [state]: emended per the Southern Supervisory edition and Yuan Gui 191.

s0367.literal: Nature and spirit together were moved: "moved" was originally corrupted to "measure"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
s0367.idiomatic: On "nature and spirit alike were moved": the text originally read measure for moved; other editions are correct; emended.

s0368.literal: As if driving rotten wood: "as if"—all editions read "truly."
s0368.idiomatic: On "as if driving rotten wood": all editions read truly for as if.
